 Dhubri : The Dhubri district administration has declared a holiday on Monday to mark Diwali and announced extensive safety and security arrangements for Kali Puja and Chhath Puja celebrations, as well. The preparations were reviewed at a meeting chaired by district commissioner Dibakar Nath. Representatives of Kali Puja and Chhath Puja committees, along with officials from the police, health, PWD, APDCL, inland water transport, fire and emergency services and the dhubri municipal board, attended the meeting. Nine Chhath Puja ghats have been identified in Dhubri town: Mela Maidan, Zila Parishad, Kachari, Jogomaya, BSF, Panchu, Free India, New and Out Signal. A joint team of officials and Chhath Puja committee representatives will inspect the ghats on November 10 or 11 to assess requirements related to repairs, lighting, sanitation, traffic management and other facilities. Boat movement will be regulated from noon on November 14 to 10 am on November 16. E-rickshaw movement in Dhubri town will also be restricted from 8 am to 3 pm on November 15 to facilitate the movement of devotees. Police will strengthen security at puja venues and ghats. Medical teams, ambulances, mobile medical units, rescue boats and State Disaster Response Force personnel will be deployed at vulnerable locations, while fire tenders will remain on standby at major congregation points. Puja committees have been asked to install CCTV cameras, deploy trained volunteers with identity cards and maintain firefighting arrangements. A round-the-clock control room will operate from Dak Bungalow during the festival period. Dhubri puja coordination committee vice-president Simul Sarkar welcomed the arrangements and urged organisers and devotees to follow administrative guidelines. Senior Chhath Puja committee member Dev Kumar stressed the need for adequate lighting, sanitation, changing rooms for women, drinking water, medical facilities and barricading at all nine ghats. District commissioner Dibakar Nath appealed to all stakeholders to cooperate with the administration to ensure peaceful, safe and harmonious celebrations.
